key_idea: Multi-source BFS where every cell stores its two best distinct towers ordered by (distance, id); the k-best of a cell always propagate through a neighbour's k-best.
sketch: Run Dijkstra/BFS over states (dist, tower id, cell) in lexicographic order; a cell accepts a state if it has fewer than 2 towers and does not already hold that id, then pushes to its 4 neighbours. Correctness: if tower t is in the top-2 of x, it is in the top-2 of the neighbour y on a shortest path to t, since anything beating t at y also beats it at x. At most 2 accepted states per cell, so about 2*4*r*c pushes, O(rc log) and 0.2s. Pitfalls: tie-breaking by lowest id for both the first and the second tower, and fast output of 500k numbers.
